overviewParagraphs: Vietnam Golf & Country Club (VGCC) is widely regarded as Vietnam’s premier golf and country club. Located just 20 kilometers from the center of Ho Chi Minh City, it offers an accessible escape into lush parkland surroundings.

The club features two championship courses. The West Course, designed by Taiwanese architect Chen King Shih, opened in 1994 and is characterized by narrow tree-lined fairways and fast greens. The East Course, designed by six-time major champion Lee Trevino, opened in 1997 and offers wider fairways with cleverly positioned hazards, providing a strategic test for players of all levels.

VGCC has hosted numerous prestigious events, including the Vietnam Open. Its mature trees, meandering waterways, and meticulously manicured grounds make it a classic, must-play destination on any Southern Vietnam golf tour.

curatorBriefHtml: Vietnam Golf & Country Club (VGCC) — located in Thu Duc City just 30–40 minutes from District 1, Ho Chi Minh City — is Southern Vietnam’s historic 36-hole flagship, opened in 1994 as the country’s first 36-hole championship club. Its two mature, tree-lined loops offer distinct personalities: the tournament-tested West Course (7,106 yards, Par 72, host of multiple Vietnam Opens) and the Lee Trevino-designed East Course (6,946 yards, Par 72), known for slightly wider fairways and bold, heavily bunkered greens.

Having played VGCC personally, its standout strength is classic maturity and proximity to central Saigon. Towering tropical trees frame every hole, creating a shaded, traditional parkland ambiance that newer open-field courses simply cannot replicate — and putting you back in District 1 by early afternoon for lunch or rooftop drinks.
VGCC is a core anchor on our Saigon & Shores Escape, pairing smoothly with Long Thanh, Taekwang Jeongsan, and The Bluffs Grand Ho Tram.

scorecard.verdict: Vietnam's first 36-hole golf club. The East Course by Lee Trevino offers generous landing areas but severely undulating greens, while the West Course tests driving accuracy through narrow tree-lined fairways.

faqs.q: Should visiting golfers play the West Course or East Course at VGCC?
faqs.a: Both are mature parkland classics. Choose the West Course (7,106 yards) for tighter, tree-lined championship shotmaking with Vietnam Open pedigree, or Lee Trevino’s East Course (6,946 yards) for slightly more generous landing zones and dramatic greenside bunkering.

faqs.q: How far is Vietnam Golf & Country Club from central Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: VGCC is one of Saigon’s closest courses — typically 30 to 45 minutes east of District 1 by private touring vehicle depending on city traffic.

faqs.q: Is VGCC suitable for mixed-handicap groups?
faqs.a: Yes. The East Course in particular offers fair landing corridors and enjoyable resort playability, while the West Course rewards straight drivers and sharp short games.

faqs.q: When is the best season to play VGCC?
faqs.a: December through April is Southern Vietnam’s dry season; during the May–November green season, morning starts (07:00–08:30 AM) enjoy lush fairways well before afternoon showers.
